meta.title: Cyber Safety Tips: Cybercrime Report & Tracking
meta.description: Practical, well-known guidance for staying safe from UPI, KYC, OTP and investment scams, and what to do if one just happened.

title: Cyber safety tips
subtitle: None of this is specific to this prototype. It's the same common-sense guidance every bank and cyber cell publishes. Read what's relevant to you; nothing here needs to be memorised.
heroImageAlt: A close-up of a hand typing on a laptop keyboard.

items.title: Never share an OTP, even with your own bank
items.body: A real bank, wallet, or delivery agent never needs the OTP you receive. It's proof for you, not for them. Anyone asking for it on a call, SMS reply, or WhatsApp message is committing fraud, no exceptions.

items.title: Check a UPI request before you approve it
items.body: A UPI "collect" request debits money from you when you accept it. It does not credit you. If someone asks you to "accept" a request to receive a refund, a prize, or a payment, that's the scam. Read the payee name and amount carefully before tapping approve.

items.title: Banks and government departments never ask for your PIN, password, or CVV
items.body: Not over a call, not over SMS, not through a link. If a caller already knows your name, last transaction, or partial card number, that doesn't make the request legitimate. It means your data was leaked elsewhere.

items.title: Be wary of unsolicited links about KYC, SIM blocking, or account suspension
items.body: Messages threatening that your SIM, bank account, or electricity connection will be blocked "within 24 hours" are designed to make you panic and click without thinking. Contact the organisation directly using a number from their official website, not the one in the message.

items.title: Verify investment and job offers independently
items.body: Guaranteed high returns, work-from-home tasks paid in advance, or stock tips from a WhatsApp/Telegram group are the standard pattern for investment fraud. Verify any trading app or advisor against SEBI's registered-intermediary list before sending money.

items.title: Keep your devices and apps updated
items.body: Security updates patch the exact vulnerabilities scammers rely on. Install apps only from official app stores, and avoid sideloading APKs sent to you directly, a common vector for banking-trojan malware.

ifItJustHappened.title: If it just happened
ifItJustHappened.body: Money was taken, or you think you're being scammed right now. There's a dedicated page that walks through exactly what to do in the next few minutes, in order.

items.title: The fake bank "KYC update" call
items.body: A caller claims your KYC has expired and account will be frozen, then asks you to install a screen-sharing app "to help update it," or to share an OTP "to verify." The screen-sharing app lets them see and operate your banking app directly.

items.title: The UPI "collect request" trick
items.body: Someone selling something online sends you a UPI collect request instead of a normal payment link, disguised as if you're the one being paid. Approving it sends money out of your account, not into it.

items.title: The "refund" or "cashback" scam
items.body: You're told a refund is due and asked to share your card details, OTP, or to accept a payment request to "process" it. No legitimate refund ever requires you to pay, approve a debit, or share an OTP.

items.title: The investment-group pump
items.body: A WhatsApp or Telegram group shows screenshots of large returns and pressures members to invest quickly in an unregistered trading app. Withdrawals stop working once enough money has been deposited.

items.title: The follow-up "investigator" call
items.body: After a real fraud happens, victims are sometimes called again by someone posing as a police officer or cyber cell investigator, asking for Aadhaar, card, or OTP details "to help recover the money." No real investigator asks for this over a call. Verify only by calling 1930 yourself.

footer: This page is general public-safety guidance, not personalised advice. See <link>what's real vs mocked</link> in this prototype for what this build actually does and doesn't do.
